LHX.sentence: L3Harris ticked up slightly, but the real issue is still that it earns thinner profit margins than the bigger defense contractors, which is why the stock has been so far below its highs.

ASML.sentence: ASML is quiet this week — it's still the only company in the world that makes a certain kind of chipmaking machine, and investors are waiting on the faster growth expected over the next couple of years.

LIN.sentence: Linde is having an uneventful stretch — selling industrial gases like oxygen and nitrogen under long contracts is a steady business, and it's priced almost in line with its nearest rival despite running the better operation.

MSFT.sentence: No fresh read on Microsoft today — nothing to report.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher dipped a touch, but biotech funding is thawing again, and since that money eventually turns into orders for their lab equipment, it's an encouraging sign for a few quarters out.

ENB.sentence: Enbridge edged higher — it runs oil and gas pipelines like a toll road and pays a steady dividend, and right now nothing unusual is happening with it.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow dropped sharply today and is well off its high, which is rare for such a steady grower — big companies and government agencies keep signing on for its workflow and AI tools, so the business story hasn't changed with the price.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore is up slightly and paying a hefty dividend, supported by its commodity-trading arm that makes money even when metal prices bounce around.

MLM.sentence: Martin Marietta rose today, and the number that matters most — the price it gets for a ton of crushed stone — is still climbing nicely, even though a shift in sales mix made the headline figure look weaker than reality.

KOF.sentence: The Latin American Coca-Cola bottler had a nice up day, with the Mexican peso sitting in its normal range, so there's nothing out of the ordinary driving it.

PBR.A.sentence: Petrobras rose as oil sits far above what it costs them to pump, which means gushing cash and a fat dividend right now — though earnings this good are hard to sustain if oil eventually cools.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk, the Danish container-shipping giant, dipped slightly, but its shares are priced below what its fleet of ships would cost to replace — the kind of bargain that shows up at the bottom of a shipping cycle.

MA.sentence: Mastercard was basically flat, and interestingly it's priced almost identically to Visa even though it's been growing a bit faster — people keep tapping their cards everywhere, every day.

ISRG.sentence: The surgical robot company was quiet today after a strong month — hospitals keep doing more operations with its machines, and every procedure means more disposable supplies sold.
